practice.title: Scenario 1 — The list re-renders on every keystroke in an unrelated field
symptoms: a 400-row table view becomes janky when typing in a filter input; the Profiler shows the row component committing on every keystroke even though no row data changed. No warnings, no errors.

(a) a context provider above the table has value={{ filters, rows }} recreated per render; (b) the store selector returns a new array/object (s.rows.filter(...)) so useSyncExternalStore sees a new snapshot every notification; (c) the filter state lives in the same context as the rows, so filtering legitimately re-renders the list; (d) React.memo rows receive an inline style={{...}} or a callback prop; (e) a parent re-render creates new element props for every row.
investigation: DevTools React panel → enable "Highlight updates when components render" → type one character → watch which component flashes. Turn on the Profiler with "Record why each component rendered" and read the recorded reason (Props changed: 'onSelect' vs Context changed). Grep for value={{ and for selectors returning .filter(/.map(. Log useSyncExternalStore snapshot identity: console.log(s === prevSnapshot) — if false on a store notification with unchanged data, the selector is allocating.
rootCause: the filter state and the row data shared one context/store subscription, and the row selector returned a fresh array, so every keystroke invalidated 400 memoised rows.
fix: split the contexts by update frequency (filters context vs data context), memoise the row selector (createSelector on byId + ids, with the filter applied outside the memo or inside a memised selector), pass stable callbacks (useCallback or a row id with a lookup), and mark rows React.memo with a custom areEqual if they carry derived fields.
prevention: a render-count assertion test (expect(renderCount).toBe(1) after an unrelated state change), a lint/codemod rule against useSelector(s => s.x.filter(...)), and a documented rule that a component subscribes to the narrowest slice and that memoised boundaries require stable inputs.

practice.title: Scenario 2 — Infinite redirect loop between /app and /login
symptoms: users with a valid session bounce between /app and /login; a handful of them land in a blank page after the loop; the server logs show a steady GET storm on both URLs. Started right after a release that added an authenticated layout route.

(a) the new loader calls your API without forwarding the Cookie/Authorization header, so the API returns 401 and the loader redirects to login; (b) a permission check requires a permissions query that itself is guarded, creating mutual recursion; (c) next is dropped so the user lands on /app instead of the original URL; (d) a session cookie is set on the redirect response but with a path/domain that excludes the API path; (e) a middleware matcher catches /login and redirects logged-in users to /app, which loops with the API check.
investigation: reproduce in a private window with DevTools open and "Preserve log" on; look at the failing XHR/fetch — is it sent with credentials? Check the request headers for Cookie/Authorization. curl -sI -H 'Cookie: __session=…' https://staging.example.com/app and the same against /api/me. Read the server access log for the *exact* repeating sequence and the status of every request in it (the 401 is the tell). Check the login redirect code for next preservation and for a ?reason marker.
rootCause: the layout loader fetched the current user without forwarding the request's auth headers, so it always saw "anonymous" and always redirected.
fix: pass request.headers.get('cookie') (or build an authHeaders(request) helper) into every loader fetch; assert credentials: 'include' for cookie-based APIs; add ?reason=session-expired so the second hop is distinguishable; add a "do not redirect twice for the same navigation" guard so a genuine failure lands on an error page instead of looping.
prevention: a helper that makes forwarding the *hard* path (a typed serverFetch(request, url) that always reads auth from the request); an integration test that deep-links to a protected route with a valid session and asserts a 200; an alert on repeated 3xx chains in the access log; and never put a permission check in a layout that a child loader also needs to fetch.

practice.title: Scenario 3 — Duplicate requests for the "same" data
symptoms: the network panel shows two identical GET /api/invoices?page=2 requests on every page change, and four on the first load of the invoice detail page. Response times are fine; nothing errors.

(a) two components build the key differently (['invoices', 2] vs ['invoices', { page: 2 }] vs ['invoices', 'page=2']); (b) one uses useQuery and the other useSWR (two caches); (c) the list uses a fetch in a useEffect *and* a query; (d) select returns a new array, causing a re-render that re-mounts the hook (unlikely, but check); (e) StrictMode double-invoking effects (dev only — verify whether this is production); (f) an SSR pass fetches on the server and the client refetches because staleTime/initialDataUpdatedAt was not set.
investigation: log every key: queryClient.getQueryCache().getAll().map(q => q.queryKey) and inspect for near-duplicates. In DevTools filter by "Fetch/XHR" and compare the full URLs *and* the initiator stack. Search the codebase for hand-written fetch( calls inside components. Check whether the duplicated requests appear in production (StrictMode) or only in dev. Look for hydrate()/initialData and confirm initialDataUpdatedAt matches the server timestamp.
rootCause: two callers used structurally different keys for the same request, so the cache treated them as distinct entries; a third came from an effect-based fetch.
fix: centralise the keys in one factory (invoiceKeys.list(page)), remove the effect fetch, use one data library per app, and set initialDataUpdatedAt (or staleTime) so the hydrated cache is not immediately stale.
prevention: key factories in a shared module; a lint rule banning useQuery([ / useSWR( with an inline array literal; a smoke test that asserts request counts with a request counter (Playwright page.on('request')); and one data library per app as an architectural rule.

practice.title: Scenario 4 — The "infinite spinner" on a route that should have 403'd
symptoms: a restricted page shows an infinite skeleton for users without permission. Network shows the request 403s within 40 ms. The user can see the route in the nav (so they know it exists) but can never load it.

(a) the component only handles isLoading and isError is being treated as isPending (TanStack Query v4→v5 isLoading rename confusion); (b) the loader throw data(...) is caught but the error boundary is only at the root and the root's boundary also spins; (c) the query has retry: (n) => n < 3 on a 403, so it retries forever with a spinner; (d) enabled is false because the permissions query has not resolved, and nothing re-enables it; (e) the error state is rendered but visually identical to the skeleton.
investigation: print query.status, isPending, isFetching, isError in the component; check the request log for repeated identical requests (retry storm); inspect the nearest ErrorBoundary in the tree (React DevTools highlights which boundary caught it); in v5 confirm you migrated isLoading → isPending everywhere (a common upgrade bug: isLoading now means "pending AND fetching", so a failed query has isLoading: false but many components wrote !isLoading ? <Error/> : <Spinner/>).
rootCause: the route had no per-route error boundary and the component treated a terminal 403 as a still-loading query, so it never left the pending branch.
fix: render the error state from isError first; make retry return false for 4xx; add an errorElement/ErrorBoundary at the route; and return a real 403 from the loader with a Forbidden view, not a thrown generic error.
prevention: a shared <AsyncBoundary> that handles loading/error/empty/partial in one place (4.4.10); a default retry that never retries 4xx; per-route error boundaries in the route table; and an e2e test that visits the restricted route as an unprivileged user and asserts the 403 view.

practice.title: Scenario 5 — Data is correct in dev, stale in production for ~3% of users
symptoms: a settings page shows the old plan for a small subset of users. Reproducible only in production; it resolves after a hard refresh. Release correlation: it started the day a new CDN rule was added.

(a) the authenticated HTML/JSON is being CDN-cached without Vary: Cookie/private — one user's response served to another; (b) the query cache is persisted (persistQueryClient) with a long TTL and the hydration path skips revalidation; (c) a service worker serves a cached API response; (d) the flag/cohort cookie is cached and the server-rendered variant disagrees with the client; (e) staleTime: Infinity with a missed invalidation.
investigation: curl -sI https://app.example.com/settings -H 'Cookie: session=userA' and inspect Cache-Control, Vary, Age, x-cache. Fetch the *exact* HTML for two different cookies and diff it — if they are identical, you have a cache-key bug. Check whether the query client is persisted and what buster/maxAge it uses. Check the service worker registration and its cache names. Compare the affected rate with the rollout percentage and with cache-age distribution.
rootCause: the CDN cached an authenticated page keyed only by URL, so a fraction of users received another user's (or an older) render.
fix: Cache-Control: private, no-store (or at minimum Vary: Cookie plus a cache-key that includes the identity) on authenticated responses; purge the affected cache paths; add the identity to the cache key for anything user-specific.
prevention: a rule that authenticated responses are never publicly cached, enforced in the CDN config and asserted by an automated check (request with a cookie, assert no-store); Vary headers in the response helper; no persisted query cache without a documented TTL and a logout clear(); and a synthetic test that requests an authenticated route with two different cookies and asserts the bodies differ.

practice.title: Scenario 6 — Optimistic like disappears when a second user also likes
symptoms: user A likes a post (instant), user B likes the same post a second later; A's UI snaps back to "not liked" for a few seconds and then returns to "liked". No errors.

(a) A's mutation is invalidated by a push event for the *same* entity from B, and the refetch response was generated before A's write committed (read-after-write inconsistency); (b) the refetch replaced the whole post object with a stale server copy; (c) a useEffect that syncs props to state overwrote the optimistic value; (d) the like count is a separate query that got invalidated and refetched with a cached intermediate value; (e) double-submission: two mutations for one click, second one 409s and rolls back.
investigation: reproduce with two browsers against staging; enable the mutation timeline in the query devtools (or add onMutate/onSuccess/onError/onSettled logs with timestamps and the incoming payload); check the server response for the refetch and compare likedBy with what the UI shows; look for two mutation calls per click (a form submit plus a click handler both firing).
rootCause: the invalidating refetch raced the mutation's own write (no read-your-writes guarantee) and its response overwrote the optimistic cache entry.
fix: ensure read-your-writes (the mutation's onSuccess writes the authoritative entity *after* any in-flight refetch, or cancel + refetch *after* settle); make the refetch a POST-invalidate if the API supports it; and guard against double submission with isPending.
prevention: the cancelQueries → optimistic → onSuccess → onSettled invalidate ordering, enforced by a shared mutation helper; an idempotency key so a double click is one write; and a two-browser e2e test for concurrent likes.

practice.title: Scenario 7 — The feed loses items when scrolling back up
symptoms: a cursor-paginated feed, maxPages: 7. Users report that scrolling up sometimes loads the same items twice and sometimes jumps a screen; on a fast scroll some items are skipped.

(a) dedupe is applied per page instead of at merge time; (b) getNextPageParam is called with a stale lastPage due to a closure in the effect; (c) maxPages sliding shifts indices so the saved cursor array no longer matches the page it does; (d) the sentinel effect fires twice concurrently (no isFetching guard) and two fetchNextPage calls interleave; (e) the server's cursor is not scoped to the filter set, so changing a filter mid-scroll mixes two cursors.
investigation: log every request URL plus the returned nextCursor and item ids; in the devtools, step through a slow scroll and watch for two concurrent requests for the same cursor; assert the merged id list has no duplicates by adding a dev-only invariant assert(new Set(ids).size === ids.length); check whether getPreviousPageParam is implemented at all (if not, "scroll up" is doing nothing while maxPages still drops pages).
rootCause: no isFetchingNextPage guard plus per-page rather than merged dedupe, with maxPages trimming pages whose cursors were still needed.
fix: guard the sentinel with hasNextPage && !isFetchingNextPage; dedupe in one useMemo over the flattened pages; keep cursors keyed by page index plus trim only on the far end; scope cursors to the filter set server-side and reset the query when filters change.
prevention: a dev invariant for duplicate ids; an e2e test that scrolls 5 screens up and down and asserts the id sequence is strictly monotonic with no duplicates; and staleTime/resetKeys discipline so a filter change starts a fresh chain.

practice.title: Scenario 8 — Flash of wrong theme on first paint
symptoms: users with dark mode enabled see a white flash for 150–400 ms on hard load, only on first navigation of the session. No hydration warnings in the console.

(a) the theme is read from localStorage in a useEffect, so the first client render uses the default; (b) the theme is in Context with value={{ theme }} created in a client component that mounts after paint; (c) a CSS prefers-color-scheme media query is used alongside an explicit toggle, and they disagree; (d) the <html> class is set by an effect on the client only; (e) the blocking head script exists but the cookie-based path is not used for SSR.
investigation: curl -s https://app.example.com/ | grep -i 'class=' on <html> — the server output must already carry the theme. Disable JavaScript and check the rendered colours. Use the Performance panel and look at the first paint vs the first contentful paint; chrome://media-internals/emulation for prefers-color-scheme. Look for two sources of truth (media query + stored preference).
rootCause: the theme is applied after hydration because it is client-read state, so the first paint uses the default palette.
fix: resolve the theme before first paint: store it in a cookie the server can read, render <html class="dark"> on the server, and add a tiny blocking inline script in <head> that sets the class from localStorage when no cookie exists (accepting the CSP cost of a nonce, 4.6.9); gate React rendering on a hydrated flag so there is no mismatch.
prevention: theme resolution in one module used by the server and the client; a visual test in both themes; and suppressHydrationWarning only on the <html> element, never globally.

practice.title: Scenario 9 — Maximum update depth exceeded after adding a store selector
symptoms: a screen throws "Maximum update depth exceeded" within a second of mount. It started when a component switched from useSelector(s => s.count) to useSelector(s => ({ a: s.a, b: s.b })).

(a) the selector returns a new object → useSyncExternalStore's snapshot differs on every call → React re-subscribes in a loop; (b) an effect that dispatches state on every render, and the dispatch notifies the same subscriber; (c) setState in the store called during render; (d) a selector that reads a mutable object whose identity is stable but whose contents the component mutates during render.
investigation: read the error stack for the repeated component. Log the snapshot identity inside getSnapshot: console.log(next === prev). Check the store's setState for an equality bail-out. Verify whether the dispatch is in an effect with an unstable dependency.
rootCause: object-literal selector output defeats useSyncExternalStore's snapshot identity check.
fix: return a primitive, use useShallow/a shallow-equality option, or memoise with createSelector.
prevention: a lint rule for inline object/array returns in selectors; a useSelector wrapper in store/hooks.ts that documents the rule; and a dev-only warning when a selector output is not Object.is-stable across two calls with the same state.

practice.title: Scenario 10 — Route guard bypass: user changes the id in the URL
symptoms: QA reports that a user can read another team's invoice by editing /invoices/123 to /invoices/124. The nav is correct and the button is hidden, but the request returns 200 with data.

(a) the API endpoint trusts the id and only checks authentication, not authorisation; (b) the loader calls requireUser (authentication) but not an ownership check (authorisation); (c) the check exists but is a role check (admin vs member) rather than an object check; (d) the query is not scoped by tenant in the WHERE clause; (e) an RSC/loader path bypasses the middleware.
investigation: curl -H 'Cookie: session=userA' https://api.example.com/invoices/124 — a 200 is the finding. Read the handler's query: does it filter orgId: session.orgId? Compare with the route guard: what does it assert? Grep the route table for every dynamic route and check each has a loader that calls the *ownership* helper.
rootCause: authentication was enforced; object-level authorisation was not (classic IDOR / broken access control, OWASP A01).
fix: scope every query by tenant and owner in the data access layer, return 404 (not 403) when the object is outside the caller's scope so existence is not leaked, and add a shared requireOwnership helper that must be called by every loader/action/handler that touches a user-owned resource.
prevention: a per-route table mapping every dynamic segment to its authorisation helper, enforced in review and by a CI grep; integration tests for every route with a "user A accesses user B's resource → 404" case; authorisation enforced in the data-access layer (so a new endpoint inherits it) rather than in handlers; and log denials for alerting.

practice.title: Scenario 11 — Analytics shows fewer page views than server logs, correlated with slow pages
symptoms: client pageview counts are ~12% below server request counts, and the gap grows with page load time. Events sent in the last second before a navigation never arrive.

(a) fetch without keepalive is aborted on unload (the 4.6.6 scenario 6 cause); (b) flush on beforeunload instead of visibilitychange (unreliable on mobile, and skipped when the bfcache is used); (c) the payload exceeds sendBeacon's size cap; (d) an ad blocker kills the collector domain silently; (e) SPA navigations never fire a pageview because the collector listens to load only.
investigation: DevTools with "Preserve log" and throttled network; watch the pending request during a navigation and look for (canceled); compare counts per page type; test the beacon path and see the gap close; check navigator.userAgent/extensions; count SPA navigations separately from full loads.
rootCause: navigation-aborted fetch calls plus no visibilitychange flush, so events in the last moments of a session are lost.
fix: sendBeacon on visibilitychange/pagehide with a fetch(..., { keepalive: true }) fallback, batched under the size cap; fire a synthetic pageview on router navigations with the navigation type.
prevention: a "no event lost on navigation" integration test; a nightly reconciliation dashboard comparing client events to server truth with an alert above 5% divergence; and the collector contract documented in the analytics spec.

practice.title: Scenario 12 — Upload hangs at 0% then fails at 60 seconds
symptoms: file uploads over ~40 MB show 0% progress, then fail with a gateway timeout at exactly 60 s. Smaller files succeed. Users report "it just stops".

(a) uploads are proxied through the app server and the ingress timeout is 60 s; (b) the progress bar is fetch-based, which never fires upload progress (so it reads 0% until completion); (c) Content-Length is not pinned and the server cannot enforce a max size; (d) the client does not chunk, so a retry restarts from zero; (e) memory: the server buffers the whole file.
investigation: reproduce with a 100 MB file and watch the request timing (TTFB vs download) and the response status/headers (504, client_max_body_size, 413). Check nginx client_max_body_size, the platform's request size/time limits, and the Lambda/API Gateway payload caps. Look at the client code for xhr.upload.onprogress (absent ⇒ (b)) and for the storage layer.
rootCause: the app server was the transport, so a 60 s ingress timeout killed large uploads, and fetch gave no upload progress to show.
fix: switch to presigned direct-to-storage PUT for anything above ~5 MB (with XHR only for the progress bar if a single PUT suffices, or S3 multipart for resumability); pin Content-Length and Content-Type in the presign so the client cannot upload more or a different type; confirm server-side afterwards (ownership, size, magic bytes, malware scan) before promoting from quarantine/ to final.
prevention: a documented upload-size policy per route (a 25 MB server cap and a 5 GB direct cap); client-side validation with a clear message; a multipart resumable path with per-part retry; and a dashboard of upload failure rates by size bucket to catch regressions in the presign path.

practice.title: -4.5 RAPID-FIRE
items: Context vs store: Context broadcasts to every consumer; a store subscribes per slice — use Context for rare changes, a store for interaction-rate changes.
Context re-render trigger: a new value object identity on every provider render, even with the same contents.
Context split rule: one provider per update frequency (identity, preferences, data) so a hot change cannot invalidate cold consumers.
useSyncExternalStore contract: getSnapshot must be pure and return an Object.is-stable value, or React re-renders forever.
Infinite render cause: a selector returning a fresh object/array literal on every call.
Selector fix: primitives, or useShallow, or a memoised createSelector with a complete dependency list.
createSlice bonus: generates action creators, action types and a reducer from one reducers object, with Immer inside.
configureStore defaults: auto-batched, DevTools integration, and a middleware chain (thunk → devtools).
createAsyncThunk helpers: condition for dedupe, rejectWithValue for your own errors, extraArgument for injected dependencies.
createSelector default: memoizeOptions with an equality function, or createSelectorCreator.
createEntityAdapter: normalised ids + entities plus selectAll/selectById/selectTotal, with sortComparer for stable order.
normalizr: flattens nested API responses into { entities, result } using schema definitions.
Zustand shape: create a hook, keep set shallow (set({ a })) or replace semantics explicit, and read with selectors to subscribe narrowly.
Zustand outside React: useStore with a selector plus subscribeWithSelector, which is what makes it usable outside components.
Jotai vs Recoil: Jotai is the maintained atom library from the same author; Recoil is archived since 2023.
atomFamily: one derived atom per parameter, so atomFamily(id) is memoised per id instead of allocating per render.
useReducer vs useState: reducer when transitions depend on previous state or have named actions; state for isolated values.
Action shape: { type, payload } with a namespaced type string (domain/thing), and never a payload containing a function.
Server state: owned by the server; the client holds a cache — treat it with a query library, not a store.
Query cache default staleTime: 0, so returning to a view refetches — override it for slowly changing reference data.
staleTime vs gcTime: freshness for serving vs retention after the last observer unmounts.
gcTime: 0 consequence: no cache between screens, so every navigation shows a skeleton.
staleTime: Infinity obligation: you own every invalidation; one miss is wrong forever.
placeholderData vs initialData: placeholderData shows data while fetching and is dropped on success; initialData is treated as real cache data and is stale from the start.
keepPreviousData: renders the prior key's data during a param change, so pagination and filters do not flash a skeleton.
select: transforms server data into view data once per key; must be pure or memoised.
Query key shape: hierarchical array, prefix first, every response-varying input included, undefined omitted, tenant scoped.
Key factory rule: one exported factory per entity so nobody hand-writes a divergent literal.
invalidateQueries: marks entries stale so active ones refetch; a mutation should invalidate what it changed, not the world.
setQueryData: writes cache directly — use it for optimistic updates and websocket-driven updates, never as a silent replacement for a fetch.
cancelQueries: the required first step of an optimistic update so no in-flight refetch overwrites the predicted value.
removeQueries: deletes an entry (logout, tenant switch) — use it for cache isolation, not for "refetch".
persistQueryClient risk: hydrates a stale cache at start; needs buster, a TTL, and a logout clear().
Cache isolation: tenant/user in the key *or* queryClient.clear() on identity change, or you leak one user's data to another.
Waterfall: request B blocked on A's render/effect; fix with Promise.all, a query layer, a router loader, or intent prefetch.
Waterfall from Suspense: await a cached query is fine, but await a never-cached one throws a promise that no component is suspended on, so nothing retries it.
useSuspenseQuery: removes the effect waterfall entirely; you must supply a Suspense boundary and an errorElement.
Prefetch vs staleTime: prefetch with staleTime: 0 to warm; prefetch with staleTime: Infinity to also make it serve-without-fetch.
onMutate order: snapshot → cancelQueries → apply optimistic value.
onSettled: invalidate after both success and failure; it is the only step that guarantees convergence.

questions.text: What is a design system, and what is it not?
questions.answer: Versioned, code-encoded decisions + governance; not a Figma file, not just a component library, not a collection of 200 components

questions.text: Explain token → primitive → component → pattern → page with an example
questions.answer: Value → raw palette → single element → a task composed of elements → a route; primitive has no product knowledge

questions.text: Why have three tiers of tokens?
questions.answer: Operational: it lets a palette or brand change without touching components, and lets you forbid primitives in product code

questions.text: How do you stop teams from using primitive tokens directly?
questions.answer: Stylelint/custom lint + a CI grep for raw hex/oklch; design-system-owned token files; code review is not enough

questions.text: Theme with CSS custom properties — why not Sass variables?
questions.answer: Runtime switching, subtree scoping, no rebuild for a brand, cascade integration; Sass variables are compile-time only

questions.text: Multi-brand theming: where do overrides live?
questions.answer: Brands override the primitive palette only; semantic layer and components stay identical; loading per-brand primitives at runtime

questions.text: What does oklch() buy you?
questions.answer: Perceptual lightness → predictable contrast, tints/shades in one line, color-mix in a perceptual space avoids grey mud; needs fallbacks

questions.text: Why is contrast asymmetric between light and dark?
questions.answer: Saturation and lightness interact differently per mode; mid-grey and saturated brand colours are the usual failures; test computed contrast in both

questions.text: Controlled vs uncontrolled components?
questions.answer: Support both: controlled when a value is passed (form libraries), internal state otherwise; both must stay in sync

questions.text: How do you stop boolean-prop explosion?
questions.answer: Replace booleans with a variant union; make contradictory states unrepresentable; prefer slots/compound components

questions.text: What is an escape hatch and why is removing it harmful?
questions.answer: className/style/data-* + slot extension points; without them consumers fork the component

questions.text: Polymorphic as: value and cost
questions.answer: Correct semantics and typing for links/buttons; costs type complexity, ref inference, and polymorphic prop type errors

questions.text: Where do data attributes fit?
questions.answer: Stable styling/inspection hooks (data-state, data-side) that avoid class specificity wars and are assertable in tests

questions.text: When do you use compound components?
questions.answer: Multi-part widgets with shared state (dialog, tabs, combobox); keeps sub-parts replaceable and the API readable

questions.text: How is accessibility built in rather than reviewed in?
questions.answer: Primitives own keyboard patterns, focus management, focus-visible token, reduced motion; a11y unit tests per primitive; manual AT pass per release

questions.text: Your Button needs a danger colour and a large size. Design the API
questions.answer: variant union + size union; justify why not color+isDanger+size+isLarge (state space, contradictions)

questions.text: Walk through a breaking change and its deprecation
questions.answer: Semver-major, codemod, dev-only runtime warning, usage scan, parallel majors, remove only at zero usage

questions.text: When is a big-bang restructure of a design system wrong?
questions.answer: When consumers cannot all migrate at once; use codemods, parallel majors, and a measured usage report

questions.text: Design system in a monorepo vs many repos?
questions.answer: Monorepo for coordinated changes and CI; multi-repo for isolation/access control; the release/upgrade process is the real cost either way

questions.text: How do you measure design system success?
questions.answer: Coverage % of UI from primitives, inconsistency count, axe violations, bundle delta per release, deprecation time-to-zero, escape-hatch usage

questions.text: When is a design system not worth building?
questions.answer: One team, high product churn, ~10 primitives and no patterns; the trigger is cost (third duplicated component), not taste

questions.text: shadcn/ui vs Radix vs MUI vs Ant vs Chakra?
questions.answer: Distribution model first (source-in-repo vs package), then headless vs styled; ownership of a11y and maintenance follows from that

questions.text: Why did copy-the-source become popular?
questions.answer: Customisation drops to a diff you control; no release train; the cost is that a11y fixes, React upgrades, and patches become your backlog

questions.text: Headless vs styled: what are you choosing?
questions.answer: Behaviour ownership vs pixel ownership; speed-to-finished-UI vs visual distinctiveness; a11y burden lands on you in headless

questions.text: How do you make a third-party component replaceable?
questions.answer: Your own API and types, adapter owns state/a11y, single import site, no leaked types, pin versions, escape hatch without pass-through

questions.text: Why is localStorage wrong for tokens?
questions.answer: Any script on the origin can read it (XSS + third-party tags); use HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite cookies with CSRF defence (PHASE 7 → Token Storage)

questions.text: Storybook: what does it do that unit tests don't?
questions.answer: Renders with real styles so play can assert layout/visibility, plus visual regression, a11y, and a human review surface

questions.text: What is a "story of stories"?
questions.answer: The coverage requirement: one story per state, not one per component — the contract that prevents untested states

questions.text: How do you make visual regression baselines stable?
questions.answer: Pin browser/platform, bundle fonts, disable animation, seed time/randomness, mask dynamic regions, wait for loaded states before asserting

questions.text: Why is a play function more than a smoke test?
questions.answer: It runs a real user (userEvent) against a styled render, so focus order, visibility, and layout are asserted; it doubles as an interaction test in CI

questions.text: What does the axe addon miss?
questions.answer: Keyboard operability, focus visibility/trapping, announcement quality, name meaningfulness, reflow/zoom, timing

questions.text: When is Storybook pure overhead?
questions.answer: One team, ~15 components, no designers involved, stories not maintained — and it is overhead if interaction tests live somewhere else

questions.text: Real motivations for micro-frontends
questions.answer: Independent deploy cadence for multiple teams, deployable ownership, incremental legacy migration, genuinely different domain lifecycles

questions.text: Costs people underestimate
questions.answer: CSS isolation compromises, dependency duplication, version skew, fragmented observability, composition-level E2E, SEO, N× pipelines

questions.text: Build-time vs runtime composition
questions.answer: Build-time is simplest and fastest but loses independent deploy; runtime (federation) needs compatibility contracts and a fallback

questions.text: How is routing owned?
questions.answer: Shell owns top-level routes and auth; MFEs own sub-routes; route manifests must be versioned; unknown-route and remote-failure states must be handled

questions.text: Which deps must be singletons and why?
questions.answer: React (hooks), router, i18n, token provider, query cache, analytics, auth client — two instances means two histories or broken hooks

questions.text: Cross-MFE communication channels ranked
questions.answer: URL/route state first, then typed DOM events, then a shared hint store, then shared packages; never import another MFE's internals

questions.text: Auth across three apps?
questions.answer: Shared HttpOnly cookie session on the parent domain, one auth client in the shell, expiry broadcast everywhere, CSRF defence

questions.text: Shell v2 with remote v1 deployed: failure modes?
questions.answer: Missing API, changed prop contracts, duplicate singletons, event schema drift, cache invalidation; mitigate with additive contracts, remote health checks, previews

questions.text: Migrate a monolith to micro-frontends: order
questions.answer: Shell last; start with one edge route, extract shared primitives first, establish contracts before MFE #2, sunset the old surface

questions.text: When should you *not* use micro-frontends?
questions.answer: <20 engineers, one team, coupling-heavy domains, no platform capacity, realtime-coherent products; modular monolith instead

questions.text: Feature-based vs type-based folders
questions.answer: Feature-based optimises deletion and co-location; type-based enables false reuse and produces dumping grounds; enforce with lint, not review

questions.text: How do you enforce dependency direction?
questions.answer: eslint-plugin-boundaries element types + rules, deep-import bans, madge --circular in CI, ratchet down existing violations

questions.text: Why do barrels hurt?
questions.answer: Larger re-export graphs make tree-shaking harder, blow up watch/build invalidation, hide cycles, and collide silently with export *

questions.text: When does shared code become a package?
questions.answer: ≥2 real consumers, a named owner, independent change cadence, and a stable public API; otherwise duplicate deliberately

questions.text: How do feature flags belong in the structure?
questions.answer: At one seam, not scattered; both branches tested in CI (matrix); owner + expiry in the definition, enforced by a CI check

questions.text: Incremental vs big-bang restructure
questions.answer: Refactors must be behaviour-preserving at every commit; move bottom-up with tests, delete the old path in the last PR

questions.text: What is the single most important Sentry detail?
questions.answer: Release tagging plus source-map upload for the *exact* deployed build; without it, stack traces are unreadable

questions.text: Unhandled vs handled error capture
questions.answer: Unhandled is the noisy baseline; handled captureException at boundaries is the highest-signal data you will ever collect

questions.text: Context that makes an error actionable
questions.answer: Release, environment, dist, user id, session id, route tag, feature-flag values, breadcrumbs, trace id

questions.text: Session replay: what must be masked?
questions.answer: All inputs and free text by default, all media, and any unaudited authenticated page; sampling by session; legal review and short retention

questions.text: How do you stop Sentry noise?
questions.answer: beforeSend filtering, custom fingerprints for shared frames, ignore list with written justification, rate-limit per release, split mis-grouped issues

questions.text: When do you page on an error?
questions.answer: New issues in a release you just shipped, high volume user-affecting regressions, error-budget burn; tickets for the rest

questions.text: What must never leave the browser?
questions.answer: PII, tokens, cookies, Authorization headers, full request bodies, full DOM of authenticated pages

questions.text: SaaS vs self-hosted Sentry
questions.answer: Start SaaS; self-host only for data residency, legal requirements, or genuine volume; the operational burden is real

questions.text: Kinds of feature flags and their lifetimes
questions.answer: Release (expires), kill switch (never expires), experiment (ends in a decision), entitlement (long-lived)

questions.text: How do you bucket a percentage rollout?
questions.answer: Deterministic hash of a stable id salted with the flag key — sticky across sessions and devices, independent across experiments

questions.text: Where should a flag be evaluated?
questions.answer: Server/edge for anything affecting markup or data (correct HTML, authoritative, cache-correct); client for presentation-only, untrusted

questions.text: Assignment vs exposure
questions.answer: Assignment = evaluated; exposure = actually rendered; analyse on exposure with a stable id, or results are diluted and biased

questions.text: Expand/contract for flags
questions.answer: Add new → dual write → backfill → switch reads behind a flag → verify → remove old; a flag does not migrate data

questions.text: Three flag-induced bugs
questions.answer: Client/server skew (mismatch + hydration), stale flags cached in a bundle or long-TTL storage, branch sharing mutable state with the stale side

questions.text: Flags and caching
questions.answer: HTML containing a variant must vary the CDN key on the cookie/header; flag-affected payloads must be in the cache key

questions.text: Event naming convention and schema versioning
questions.answer: Past-tense object.action (or verb-noun) consistently; schema_version in every event; never repurpose a name

questions.text: Client vs server analytics
questions.answer: Client for interaction and CWV, server for truth (revenue, entitlements); join on a shared id and reconcile

questions.text: What is a tracking plan?
questions.answer: Question → decision → funnel → event spec (name, typed props, owner, version) → storage/retention; owner approves new events

questions.text: Identity stitching and where it breaks
questions.answer: Anonymous id → identify on login; breaks on shared devices, logout, clearing cookies, multi-account households — say so honestly

questions.text: Consent: where must the gate live?
questions.answer: In the collector itself, not at call sites, so no event can escape; withdrawable as easily as given; DNT alone is not sufficient legally

questions.text: Why are events lost on navigation?
questions.answer: fetch without keepalive is aborted on unload; use sendBeacon on visibilitychange/pagehide, batched

questions.text: How do you keep analytics out of INP?
questions.answer: Fire-and-forget, never awaited; flush on visibility change; keep the collector off the interaction path and small

questions.text: Where does React's escaping stop?
questions.answer: dangerouslySetInnerHTML, URLs in href, prop spreading, user-authored rich text, direct DOM APIs, third-party embeds, postMessage

questions.text: Safe pipeline for user markdown
questions.answer: html: false parser → AST → React elements; no raw HTML passthrough; normalise at render time; sanitize at output, not write

questions.text: Why does unsafe-inline defeat CSP?
questions.answer: Injected inline scripts become allowed, so CSP no longer blocks the thing it exists to block

questions.text: Nonce CSP with strict-dynamic
questions.answer: Per-response random nonce on every script tag; strict-dynamic lets nonced scripts load further scripts (including from CDNs) so third parties stay without unsafe-*

questions.text: How do you roll out CSP safely?
questions.answer: Report-only with a monitored violation endpoint, fix violations, then enforce; document inline-style policy explicitly

questions.text: Risk of a third-party tag and how to contain it
questions.answer: Arbitrary JS with your origin's privileges; mitigate by not loading it, isolating it in a sandboxed cross-origin iframe with postMessage, allow-listing in CSP, and monitoring

questions.text: "We hide the button, so it's secure" — your response
questions.answer: Client authorization is UX only; the server must enforce per object (PHASE 7 → Broken Access Control/IDOR); IDs in URLs are untrusted

questions.text: X-Frame-Options vs frame-ancestors
questions.answer: Legacy binary header vs CSP directive that can express an origin allowlist; use frame-ancestors (and ship SAMEORIGIN for old browsers)

questions.text: Why is VITE_API_KEY not a secret?
questions.answer: It is inlined into the public bundle at build time and readable by anyone; scope/rotate/limit server-side, keep secrets off the client

questions.text: Dependency confusion vs typosquatting
questions.answer: Public package shadowing an internal name (fix: scope + registry config + npm ci) vs a name spelled like a popular package (fix: verify provenance before adding)

questions.text: What can npm audit not tell you?
questions.answer: Reachability, real exploitability, transitive business criticality; it has high noise, so allow-list with expiry and add reachability-aware review

questions.text: Handling a 429
questions.answer: Client: read Retry-After, message the user, queue/back off, never tight-loop; server: authoritative per-identity limits with a shared store

questions.text: Vue's reactivity in two sentences
questions.answer: Proxy-based ref/reactive; reads inside a reactive scope are tracked, writes re-run that scope; component render tracks its dynamic dependencies

questions.text: What does Angular's DI give you that React lacks?
questions.answer: Hierarchical, tree-shakable DI with explicit provider scoping — a convention that removes per-component decisions at large team size

questions.text: Why does Svelte have no virtual DOM?
questions.answer: The compiler emits direct DOM mutations, so no diffing runtime and a much smaller bundle; trade-off is less dynamic flexibility

questions.text: Why React? Honest answer
questions.answer: Ecosystem, hiring, RN leverage, unidirectional data flow, concurrent features — plus the honest counter-cases (Vue reactivity, Svelte runtime, Angular conventions)

questions.text: Which framework for a low-bandwidth market?
questions.answer: Requirements first: bundle/runtime budget and team skill; Vue or Svelte for lean bundles; do not pay React's ecosystem cost you will not use

questions.text: Design a typeahead: debounce and cancellation
questions.answer: Debounce ~150 ms, AbortController to cancel, request-id check to drop stale responses, LRU query cache, keep last results visible while loading

questions.text: Typeahead a11y essentials
questions.answer: role="combobox" with aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant; focus stays in the input; listbox/option/group; polite live region for counts

questions.text: Why cursors over offsets in a feed?
questions.answer: Mutating data makes offsets duplicate and skip rows; cursors are stable, and you need a backward cursor to prepend

questions.text: Scroll restoration that actually works
questions.answer: Anchor by item id + offset (not scrollY), render until the anchor exists, then measure and adjust; disable native restoration

questions.text: Optimistic updates: when and how
questions.answer: Idempotent writes with a client id, dedupe by id on ack, rollback only when safe (no server state), never for irreversible actions

questions.text: Virtualisation trade-offs
questions.answer: Row-height measurement vs fixed height, scroll-anchor instability, accessibility of off-screen content, find-in-page over virtualised rows

questions.text: Offline-first: which operations need conflict handling?
questions.answer: Only writes; reads come from the local replica. Need idempotency keys, tombstones, and a documented conflict policy per entity

questions.text: Chat: resync after reconnect
questions.answer: Re-subscribe *and* GET messages?since=<lastSeq>, then reconcile the outbox using stable client ids

questions.text: Chat a11y essentials
questions.answer: role="log" with aria-relevant="additions", polite announcements for new messages only, focusable log, timestamps with <time>, typing indicator discoverable not chatty

questions.text: CRDT vs OT
questions.answer: CRDT: commutative/idempotent merge, free cursors and offline, higher build cost and tombstone overhead. OT: cheaper to ship online, central authority, transforms per op pair are fiddly

questions.text: Undo in a collaborative editor
questions.answer: Undo *your own* actions by deleting surviving characters in the recorded intent range, not by inverse operations against current state

questions.text: Dashboard performance at 100k rows
questions.answer: Aggregate server-side, paginate/sort server-side, virtualise ~40 rows, bucket charts to ≤500 points, memoise Intl formatters

questions.text: Dashboard caching and consistency
questions.answer: Materialised aggregates, a tenant-day dataVersion so all views agree, short TTLs, "updated HH:MM" labels, never cache per-user filtered results across users

practice.title: Scenario 1 — The design system is leaking into the app
symptoms: Button renders correctly in Storybook but wrong in production: wrong padding, missing hover, dark-mode colours wrong on one screen only. Meanwhile one feature team has added !important overrides in eight files and the CSS bundle grew 40 kB.

(a) a feature bypassed the semantic tier and referenced a primitive token, so its surface ignores dark mode; (b) a global CSS reset leaked out of a feature's co-located file (a .container or button {} rule in a global stylesheet); (c) specificity conflict with a utility class that lands *after* the component stylesheet; (d) an un-scoped style in the copied components/ui file; (e) a hard-coded #hex introduced under deadline.
investigation: DevTools computed styles on the failing element → walk up the cascade to find which rule wins (in the "Styles" pane, the winning rule is struck-through-in-reverse: greyed-out rules lost); check whether the value came from a custom property and what that property resolves to; grep -rn "#[0-9a-f]\{3,6\}" src/ and grep -rn "var(--blue\|var(--gray" src/; check stylesheet order in the network panel; reproduce in Storybook with the *production* bundle (vite build && vite preview) — if it only breaks in the built app, suspect order or tree-shaken CSS.
fix: replace primitive references with semantic tokens; move feature styles into CSS Modules/scoped blocks; remove global element selectors from component CSS (use :where() for zero-specificity defaults so utilities can override intentionally); delete the !important overrides by adding the missing token/size instead; if the CSS grew, find which component pulled a new global sheet.
prevention: the tier lint plus the raw-colour CI check (4.6.1), visual regression on every primitive in both themes, size-limit on the UI package, a documented rule that primitives never style bare elements globally, and code ownership of packages/ui.
tools: browser computed styles + CSS custom-property inspector, stylelint (declaration-property-value-disallowed-list, no-descending-specificity), the CI token check from 4.6.1, CSS Modules scoping review, bundle analyzer for the growth, visual regression on the design-system stories.
practice.markdown:
**Symptoms:** `Button` renders correctly in Storybook but wrong in production: wrong padding, missing hover, dark-mode colours wrong on one screen only. Meanwhile one feature team has added `!important` overrides in eight files and the CSS bundle grew 40 kB.

**Likely causes:** (a) a feature bypassed the semantic tier and referenced a primitive token, so its surface ignores dark mode; (b) a global CSS reset leaked out of a feature's co-located file (a `.container` or `button {}` rule in a global stylesheet); (c) specificity conflict with a utility class that lands *after* the component stylesheet; (d) an un-scoped style in the copied `components/ui` file; (e) a hard-coded `#hex` introduced under deadline.

**Investigation:** DevTools computed styles on the failing element → walk up the cascade to find which rule wins (in the "Styles" pane, the winning rule is struck-through-in-reverse: greyed-out rules lost); check whether the value came from a custom property and what that property resolves to; `grep -rn "#[0-9a-f]\{3,6\}" src/` and `grep -rn "var(--blue\|var(--gray" src/`; check stylesheet order in the network panel; reproduce in Storybook with the *production* bundle (`vite build && vite preview`) — if it only breaks in the built app, suspect order or tree-shaken CSS.

**Tools:** browser computed styles + CSS custom-property inspector, stylelint (`declaration-property-value-disallowed-list`, `no-descending-specificity`), the CI token check from 4.6.1, CSS Modules scoping review, bundle analyzer for the growth, visual regression on the design-system stories.

**Fix:** replace primitive references with semantic tokens; move feature styles into CSS Modules/scoped blocks; remove global element selectors from component CSS (use `:where()` for zero-specificity defaults so utilities can override intentionally); delete the `!important` overrides by adding the missing token/size instead; if the CSS grew, find which component pulled a new global sheet.

**Prevention:** the tier lint plus the raw-colour CI check (4.6.1), visual regression on every primitive in both themes, `size-limit` on the UI package, a documented rule that primitives never style bare elements globally, and code ownership of `packages/ui`.

practice.title: Scenario 2 — Micro-frontend version skew after a shell release
symptoms: after the shell released v2, users who load a cached remote v1 see a blank /reports route, a console error about an undefined context, and duplicated React warning ("Invalid hook call" in one route only). Some users are fine.

the shell v2 stopped providing a context the remote v1 consumed; the shared singleton negotiation loaded two React copies (version ranges did not overlap); the shell's route manifest changed a prefix the remote still claims; a shared component prop changed type without being additive.
investigation: reproduce with the shell pinned at v2 and the remote pinned at v1 (preview environment with pinned versions — this is why you have one); check window for two React instances (__REACT_DEVTOOLS_GLOBAL_HOOK__ registration count, or a Symbol.for('react')/duplicate-key warning in the console); read the console error's stack for which context is missing; check the release manifests: which shell version introduced/removed the context; correlate the affected-user rate with the shell release adoption curve and with cache age.
fix: restore the context in the shell with a deprecation shim (additive, not a breaking change) and keep both majors alive; tighten requiredVersion with singleton: true and an explicit range so a mismatch throws loudly at load instead of silently duplicating; add a remote-load timeout + retry + a user-visible fallback panel so a broken remote never blanks a route.
prevention: a compatibility contract (additive-only within a major), versioned route manifests and event schemas, an integration test matrix in CI that boots the current shell against N-1 and N-2 remotes, and a per-MFE version tag on every error and metric so skew is detectable from telemetry.
tools: preview environment with pinned remote versions, federation shared config with requiredVersion/singleton, Sentry release + mf_version tags (4.6.6), postMessage event schema versioning, cross-repo usage dashboards.
practice.markdown:
**Symptoms:** after the shell released v2, users who load a cached remote v1 see a blank `/reports` route, a console error about an undefined context, and duplicated React warning ("Invalid hook call" in one route only). Some users are fine.

**Likely causes:** the shell v2 stopped providing a context the remote v1 consumed; the shared singleton negotiation loaded two React copies (version ranges did not overlap); the shell's route manifest changed a prefix the remote still claims; a shared component prop changed type without being additive.

**Investigation:** reproduce with the shell pinned at v2 and the remote pinned at v1 (preview environment with pinned versions — this is why you have one); check `window` for two React instances (`__REACT_DEVTOOLS_GLOBAL_HOOK__` registration count, or a `Symbol.for('react')`/duplicate-key warning in the console); read the console error's stack for which context is missing; check the release manifests: which shell version introduced/removed the context; correlate the affected-user rate with the shell release adoption curve and with cache age.

**Tools:** preview environment with pinned remote versions, federation `shared` config with `requiredVersion`/`singleton`, Sentry release + `mf_version` tags (4.6.6), `postMessage` event schema versioning, cross-repo usage dashboards.

**Fix:** restore the context in the shell with a deprecation shim (additive, not a breaking change) and keep both majors alive; tighten `requiredVersion` with `singleton: true` and an explicit range so a mismatch throws loudly at load instead of silently duplicating; add a remote-load timeout + retry + a user-visible fallback panel so a broken remote never blanks a route.

**Prevention:** a compatibility contract (additive-only within a major), versioned route manifests and event schemas, an integration test matrix in CI that boots the current shell against N-1 and N-2 remotes, and a per-MFE `version` tag on every error and metric so skew is detectable from telemetry.

practice.title: Scenario 3 — Storybook drift
symptoms: Storybook stories render, but several fail at runtime in the app: a story uses a prop removed last month, another depends on a mock that no longer exists, and one component has no story for its loading state.

props were removed without updating stories; stories import dev/mockData which was deleted or moved; new states were added without stories; a story passes a value that no longer type-checks because args are loosely typed.
investigation: run the storybook build and the test-runner in CI and read failures (this should already fail — if it does not, the pipeline is the bug); madge/grep for imports of deleted modules; for the missing state, diff the component's props union against the exported story list.
fix: fix the failing stories immediately; type story args strictly (satisfies Story) so a prop change becomes a type error; add missing state stories; delete stories in the same PR as prop removals (add a CI check for props removed but still referenced).
prevention: run interaction tests on every story in CI (rot becomes a failing test, not a lie), gate new components on having at least the required state stories, keep stories next to the component in the same directory and PR, and make npm run storybook:build a required status check.
tools: Storybook test-runner with play functions, vitest/jest with stories as a test suite, a custom check comparing component.__docgenInfo props to story usage, an ESLint no-restricted-syntax rule flagging deprecated props inside *.stories.*, Storybook 8/9 component-docs metadata as the source of the prop table.

practice.title: Scenario 4 — Sentry noise and false positives
symptoms: 3,000 events/day, ~40 distinct issues, and 8 people have muted the channel. Two issues have 900 events each from completely different bugs. The top issues are all ChunkLoadError from the weekly deploy window.

shared frames (router wrapper, API client) create mega-issues; beforeSend does not filter infrastructure noise; deploy-time chunk-load errors are already handled by a retry boundary so they are duplicate reports; ad blockers/network extensions trigger abort errors; one user's corrupted session generates thousands of events.
investigation: group by fingerprint and by release; for a mega-issue, look at the *variety* of messages and breadcrumbs under the same top frame; check tags for user/session concentration (a single session.id dominating = a loop, not a bug); check the timestamp distribution against deploy windows; ask whether the retry boundary actually caught the error (if it did, captureException there is redundant).
fix: filter handled-and-recovered errors (ChunkLoadError inside the retry boundary returns null); split the mega-issues with a custom fingerprint including the operation type; rate-limit repeats after N occurrences per issue; add a session-based circuit breaker client-side (Sentry.getCurrentHub().bindClient skip after 50 events in a session); delete noise issues with a written justification.
prevention: adopt "alert on new issues in a release you just shipped" instead of "alert on any event"; keep the ignore list small and reviewed; write a definition of a *handled* error (anything you recovered from does not get reported, or is reported with level: 'log'); measure alert-to-action ratio quarterly and delete channels that nobody acts on.
tools: beforeSend/beforeBreadcrumb filters, custom fingerprint, per-issue rate limiting, Sentry inbound filters and ignore lists, denyUrls for known extensions, dashboards for event volume per issue and per user.

practice.title: Scenario 5 — Flag-induced flash of wrong content
symptoms: ~3% of users briefly see the old checkout layout, then it swaps to the new one. No errors. Analytics show a spike in checkout_step_viewed with the new step names and then a repeat with old names.

the server rendered with the flag off and the client evaluated it on (hydration mismatch, then React re-renders); the flag value is cached in localStorage with a long TTL while the server uses live config; the CDN cached the HTML for the other variant; the bundle was built with a build-time flag default baked in (VITE_FLAG_*) while production config says otherwise.
investigation: reproduce with a cold cache and with the flag flipped in a preview environment; inspect the served HTML (curl -H 'Cookie: …') for the variant markup and compare with the client-evaluated value; check the CDN Vary/Cache-Control headers and the cache key; check whether the flag value appears as a literal in the built JS (grep the bundle); compare affected-user rate with rollout percentage (3% ≈ the off-cohort).
fix: evaluate the variant on the server for anything markup-affecting and pass it down as initial state (<div data-variant="b"> or a serialised config), so the first client render matches; remove build-time inlining of flag values; reduce the flag TTL to minutes and revalidate on route change; add the variant (and, for personalised pages, the cookie/header) to the CDN cache key; until fixed, force the flag to 0% to stop the flash.
prevention: a rule that flags affecting markup/data are server-evaluated and included in the cache key; a test that asserts server HTML equals the hydrated tree for both variants; a CI check that fails if a flag name appears as an inlined literal in a build; a dashboard of variant distribution by page view (the flash shows up as a duplicate-funnel artifact).
tools: curl/view-source plus Cache-Control inspection, the bundle grep for inlined values, hydration-mismatch console warnings, flag exposure events with variant (4.6.8), Sentry flags tag on errors, a synthetic check from two regions.

practice.title: Scenario 6 — Analytics events lost on navigation
symptoms: the funnel's last-step counts are consistently ~15% below backend order counts, and the gap grows with page load. Events sent via fetch in the last 800 ms before a navigation vanish. No errors appear.

fetch without keepalive is aborted when the document unloads; flushing on a route change *after* navigation started; events flushed on beforeunload (unreliable on mobile and when a bfcache/kill occurs); no visibilitychange handler; a single large payload exceeding sendBeacon's size limit; an ad blocker blocking the collector domain (check with the request failing silently).
investigation: DevTools network with "Preserve log" and throttled network → watch the pending request during a navigation; compare client-side counts to a backend count for the same window (quantify the gap per page type); check whether the failing requests appear as (canceled); test with the beacon path and see the gap close.
fix: switch the flush path to sendBeacon with the keepalive fallback, flush on visibilitychange (not just unload), batch to stay under the cap, and treat analytics as fire-and-forget everywhere (never await).
prevention: a "no event lost on navigation" integration test (fire an event, navigate immediately, assert arrival at a local collector); a nightly reconciliation dashboard comparing client events to server truth with an alert on >5% divergence; document the collector contract (batching, cap, retry policy) and keep it in the analytics PRD rather than tribal knowledge.
tools: navigator.sendBeacon on visibilitychange/pagehide, fetch(..., { keepalive: true }) fallback, batching with a queue cap, sendBeacon size limits (~64 kB in practice → split), a local collector debug mode that prints instead of sending, a backend reconciliation report comparing counts by day.

practice.title: Scenario 7 — CSP breaks a third-party widget
symptoms: after enabling script-src 'self' in report-only mode, the console shows hundreds of violations for https://cdn.vendor.com/widget.js; the support chat widget and the payments iframe do not load. The payments flow also fails in production where CSP became enforcing.

the widget loads scripts from a CDN that is not in script-src; it injects inline scripts and inline styles (needs 'unsafe-inline' or a nonce it cannot have); it creates a blob/worker URL (blob: missing from script-src); frame-src/child-src is missing for the iframe; connect-src missing for the widget's API; the nonce was applied to your scripts but the CSP used hashes instead, so nothing is trusted.
investigation: read the CSP violation reports (they include blocked-URI, violated-directive, and sample/line numbers via the report-sample directive); enumerate the vendor's real requirements from their documentation and from the network panel on an un-CSP'd page; check report-sample so violations include the offending snippet; verify the nonce length/entropy and that it is per-response, not per-session.
fix: nonce-based script-src 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic' so the vendor's dynamically loaded scripts are allowed as descendants of your trusted bundle; add the vendor's data/API origins to connect-src, img-src, font-src; add the iframe origin to frame-src; keep 'unsafe-inline' out of script-src — if the widget needs inline scripts, isolate it in a sandboxed cross-origin iframe and communicate by postMessage.
prevention: a CSP change checklist (report-only → monitor → fix → enforce) with an owner; vendor contracts reviewed before a widget is added; a standing rule that any new third-party script requires a CSP change reviewed by whoever owns security; and alerts on unexpected violation volume (an attacker's injected script shows up as a new violation pattern).
tools: Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only + a report collector (4.6.8 collector or the Sentry breadcrumb pipeline), strict-dynamic with a nonce on your entry script (lets trusted scripts load further scripts, including from other origins, without listing them), frame-src/child-src for the iframe origin, report-sample for actionable violations, SRI where the vendor serves immutable assets.

practice.title: Scenario 8 — The bundle grew 30% after a dependency update
symptoms: after a routine dependency bump in CI, the main chunk grows 118 kB → 154 kB gzipped and LCP regresses ~400 ms. Nothing in our source changed.

the new version added a side-effectful module or removed sideEffects metadata from package.json (bundlers then keep everything); a deep import changed to a barrel path (pkg → pkg/dist/index.js), pulling the whole library; the dependency now ships a different module format (CJS instead of ESM) which disables tree-shaking; a peer dependency pulled in a polyfill that used to be excluded; the update changed a peer range so a duplicate copy is now installed; a build config change (minifier settings, manualChunks, or dropping treeshake.moduleSideEffects).
investigation: run the bundler's visualizer and diff the module list against the previous build (--stats diff or two analyzer uploads); check the lockfile diff for duplicates (npm ls <pkg> shows two versions); inspect the dependency's package.json for module/exports/sideEffects; test by pinning back one version at a time (npm i pkg@prev) to confirm causation; check whether a manualChunks split disappeared (a chunk rename can make everything appear merged into the entry).
fix: restore the deep import path if the update broke tree-shaking; add an explicit sideEffects allow-list in your own package if your metadata is the problem; keep a size-limit budget so a 30% increase fails the PR; if the library genuinely grew, replace it or lazy-load the affected feature.
prevention: dependency updates in small PRs with the size gate in CI; a CODEOWNERS-reviewed lockfile; add a renovate/dependabot config with grouped minor updates so a single major does not land silently; monitor the trend, not just the threshold (a slow 2%/month creep is the real story).
tools: bundle analyzer / stats diff, npm ls for duplicates, size-limit or a bundle-size CI gate with a diff comment on PRs, arethetypeswrong-style module checks, a lockfile-diff review step in CI, vite build --mode production reproducibility.

practice.title: Scenario 9 — Memory growth from session replay / long sessions
symptoms: a dashboard tab left open for hours grows to 4 GB, then crashes. Growth correlates with session replay enabled and with the feed being scrolled for a long time.

replay buffers unbounded DOM mutation records; the feed keeps appending items to state without ever trimming (no cap, no eviction); an IntersectionObserver/listener registered per appended row and never disconnected; a Map/Set accumulating every id ever seen with no eviction; an object-URL leak (blobs created per image preview and never revokeObjectURL'd); an event listener on window added per component instance (Phase 4.1 effect-cleanup bug) — cross-ref 4.1.7.
investigation: DevTools heap snapshots over time (take at minute 1 and minute 30; compare retained size and the biggest constructors); performance.memory/chrome://memory for a rough trend; Performance panel for allocation spikes during scroll; search the code for addEventListener, new Map(), new Set(), URL.createObjectURL without a matching cleanup; check replay configuration for retention/buffer limits.
fix: cap the feed state (retain a window plus a cursor to load older from the server) and evict the seen set alongside; virtualise so off-screen rows unmount (this is the real fix for unbounded growth); pass an AbortController signal to every listener and abort on cleanup; revokeObjectURL on preview teardown; cap replay sampling and buffer size and turn off replay for the heaviest routes.
prevention: a memory budget test — an e2e test that scrolls for N minutes and asserts JS heap stays under a threshold (this catches regressions permanently); ESLint rule or a lint check flagging addEventListener without an AbortSignal; cap state sizes by design (a feed has a max window, a cache has an LRU); document the eviction policy for every long-lived collection.
tools: heap snapshots and the "allocation timeline", Chrome Task Manager (JS heap per tab), performance.mark/measure around scroll, Map/Set with an LRU wrapper, WeakMap for per-object metadata, AbortController for listener groups.

practice.title: Scenario 10 — Keyboard trap in a modal from a library
items: Bonus scenario — "the page is slow only for users"
symptoms: a third-party dialog can be opened but not exited with the keyboard; Tab cycles inside it forever, and Escape does nothing on one route. Users with screen readers report being "trapped".

the library's dialog is nested inside another focus trap (our app modal + their modal), so the outer trap re-grabs focus after the inner closes; the Escape handler is attached to the document and another handler calls stopPropagation; the component is rendered in a portal *outside* the app's dialog root, so our global trap sees no focus and keeps cycling; inert/aria-hidden on the shell is applied while the dialog is open (from an a11y utility) and never removed, and something falls back to a brute-force trap.
investigation: keyboard-only walkthrough with the focus visible (Tab/Shift+Tab/Escape) and note where focus goes; document.activeElement logged after each Tab to see the cycle; check for nested [role="dialog"] elements in the DOM (document.querySelectorAll('[role="dialog"]').length); search the code for addEventListener('keydown' on document and for preventDefault on Tab; check whether the library expects a container/disableOutsideClickEvents/disableEscapeKeyDown option — most headless libraries expose exactly these escape hatches.
fix: wrap the third-party dialog in our own primitive so *we* own the trap contract (open/close, focus restore, Escape, scroll lock, nested-dialog stack); keep a modal stack so only the top-most dialog traps focus; ensure the portal container is inside the app root or that the app's trap is suspended while any dialog is open; explicitly restore focus to the trigger on close.
prevention: a single owned dialog primitive (4.6.1/4.6.2) with the escape hatches documented; a ModalStackProvider that suspends outer traps; a mandatory keyboard e2e per dialog story using Storybook play (4.6.3) — Tab until focus leaves, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger; an a11y review checklist item that cannot be waived for third-party overlays; and remember the axe limit: automated tools catch roughly a third of these.
tools: our own dialog primitive built on a well-tested headless library (4.6.2), with onCloseAutoFocus, disableEscapeKeyDown, trapFocus options; a debug utility that renders a visible focus ring and logs focus moves; axe (which will not catch this — say so); a keyboard-only e2e test per modal pattern; Playwright's keyboard.press('Tab') loops in a test to assert you can escape.

practice.title: PHASE 4 FINAL READINESS CHECKLIST
items: React mechanics (4.1)
[ ] I can explain the render/commit phases and name what actually triggers a re-render
[ ] I can debug stale closures and dependency arrays by reading the effect, not by trial and error
[ ] I know when an effect is unnecessary and can restate it as an event handler
[ ] I can explain useMemo/useCallback trade-offs, and when memoisation costs more than it saves
[ ] I can place useLayoutEffect vs useEffect correctly (measurement/paint vs async side effects)
[ ] I understand Context re-render propagation and how to split value and dispatch
[ ] I can use Suspense, transitions, useDeferredValue, and error boundaries correctly
[ ] I know React 19's Actions, use, useOptimistic, useFormStatus, and what the compiler changes
Patterns, styling, forms, routing, state (4.2–4.5)
[ ] I can choose composition vs configuration, and know the compound-component trade-off
[ ] I can design a CSS architecture (Modules/Tailwind/tokens) and say how it interacts with specificity
[ ] I can build a form with a schema shared by client and server, and handle server-side validation errors
[ ] I can explain routing, layouts, and code splitting at route boundaries, and lazy-load correctly

topics.title: Server components
topics.description: A Server Component renders to HTML on the server (or at build time) and its code never reaches the browser. A Client Component is normal React: it ships JavaScript, runs in the browser, and can use state, effects, and event handlers. "use client" is a *module directive*, not a component decorator. It marks the file and every module it imports as part of the client bundle. Everything a module transitively imports becomes client code. This single fact explains most "why did my bundle explode" incidents.
